label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1, late in episode (trial >= 90), previous trial rewarded
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (in_action=2, in_state=S1; 99.4% recall for that condition alone, but precision only 6%). It is also gated by episode position: it never fires before trial 80, and 97% of activation mass is in trials 90-99 (adding ep_trial>=90 raises precision to 56%). Requiring that the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward==1) brings precision to 85% (dev F1 0.87). Every variable is observed at D2: this trial choice and the reached state are shown, and the previous reward was seen at D1. Activation is weakest near the trial-90 boundary: ep_trial>=85 keeps 99.7% of mass, but low-quartile coverage drops at the >=90 cutoff, which fits a ramp with episode time. Co-occurs with low value (all activations are in the bottom value bin) and a strongly a2-leaning policy. Never fires at D1/GO, after a1, after common transitions, or when S2 is reached.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the predicate's FPs are concentrated where the previous trial reached S1. Restricted to prev_state == 1, the original predicate has dev precision 0.23 (372 predicted, about 286 FPs, roughly half of the 538 total FPs). With prev_state == 2 precision is 0.93, and on the window's first trial (prev_state unknown) it is 0.85. So the feature fires when the previous trial's reward came from S2 and this trial a2 rarely lands in S1. 'Previous trial rewarded' alone overclaims.
Adding (prev_state != 1) raises dev F1 from 0.872 to 0.896 and test F1 from 0.863 to 0.892 (test precision 0.812 -> 0.895, recall 0.922 -> 0.888, mass recall 0.973).

The core claims hold. All activation is at D2 (D1 and GO: 0 activations). Activations are 100% after action a2 and 0 before trial 80. a2 & S1 at D2 has recall 0.994 and precision 0.060. Adding ep_trial >= 90 gives precision 0.556. The original predicate scores dev F1 0.872 and test F1 0.863, as reported.
'Never fires when S2 is reached / after a common transition' is not strictly true: there are 19 activations at a2 -> S2 common (0.6% of active steps, 0.04% of mass). This is negligible.
The value-head claim ('lowest value-head bin') cannot be checked: the value quantile table in the profile is empty, and value < 0 never holds on predicate steps.
Missed activations are mostly low-magnitude, near the trial-89/90 boundary or slightly off-pattern, and hold only 2.8% of the mass. This looks like scattered noise.
